speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You've presented with fatigue, abdominal pain, night sweats, weight loss, and enlarged supraclavicular lymph nodes; to begin my evaluation, have you noticed any recent fever or changes in your bowel habits?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for confirming the timeline and severity of your symptoms. Given the combination of constitutional symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss) and supraclavicular lymphadenopathy, I need to evaluate for possible malignancy or chronic infection. Please tell me if you have experienced any cough, shortness of breath, or changes in your skin?

speaker: Patient
text: I noticed swelling in my neck over the last few days. It does not hurt, but it feels enlarged and fixed.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Hodgkin Lymphoma.

The combination of persistent constitutional symptoms (night sweats, weight loss, fatigue), abdominal pain, and specifically a painless, fixed supraclavicular lymph node is highly suggestive of a malignancy, most likely Hodgkin Lymphoma. I have already used my question allowance; please await further evaluation.
